Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to start the onboarding with Redwood. Before we jump into model pins and traffic shaping, the execs want to make sure we have a concrete plan to control token spend while meeting our 150ms median latency target for customer-facing completions.

Two quick asks for the kickoff:
- Walk us through batching and how it impacts tail latency for ~50 qps of mixed chat + generation traffic.
- Discuss KV/prefix caching for repeated user prompts and expected cost savings.
- Understand recommended quantization profiles (we're currently on open-llama-13b fp16) and tradeoffs for int8.
- Clarify routing/fallback policy behavior if a dedicated pool is saturated (we need to avoid silent throttles).

I attached a small traffic sample (anonymized). Can we schedule a 45 minute call this week? Prefer Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks all — good discussion this morning. Summarizing the technical plan and owners so we have something actionable: 

1) Batching policy (owner: Ben)
- Start with conservative dynamic batching: 25ms max-wait, target batch size tuned to keep median latency <150ms on p50/p90 for mixed workload.
- For short-chat routes, create a low-latency lane (smaller max-wait and priority scheduling).
- Deliverable: bench results comparing no-batch / 25ms / 50ms in staging by 2027-05-10.

2) KV/prefix caching (owner: Monica)
- Enable prefix cache for repeated prompts; initial TTL 24h, monitor hit-rate. Expect 20–30% token reduction on chat-heavy routes.
- Deliverable: retained hit-rate dashboard on Redwood Console + alert if hit-rate <10% after 2 weeks.

3) Quantization profile trials (owner: Rishi)
- Test open-llama-13b fp16 baseline vs int8 and a mixed-quant (kv-cache friendly) variant. Run automatic evals on our eval harness (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) and a small A/B with 5% traffic.
- Deliverable: fidelity matrix + recommendations by 2027-05-14.

4) Routing & fallback policy (owner: Ben + Neha)
- Policy: prefer dedicated pool; if saturated, route to a verified variant with explicit header indicating fallback. For critical routes, we can opt-in to blocking fallback (return 503) for first 10s to avoid silent quality drop.
- Add per-route observability so the customer sees fallback counts and avg latency per model variant.

5) Procurement cost scenarios (owner: Monica)
- We'll provide modeled unit costs for base / +25% / +100% traffic shapes using the cost-profile template. Monica to post estimated monthly $/M tokens and projected savings from caching/quantization.

Attachments from today: bench-plan.md (notes & candidate benchmark commands).

Next steps: Ben will upload preliminary bench results to the shared Drive; Rishi will kick off quant trials; Monica will produce the cost scenario spreadsheet and share by EOD 05/06.  We'll sync for a 30m follow-up on 05/12.

—
